edge_explainer: The task asked whether the 0.27 P/B is a unit or data artifact. It is NEITHER, and finding that out is what makes the real answer interesting. Price 290.2p (IBKR live) against FY25 net assets of GBP3,324.6m over 320.04m shares = GBP10.39 book per share; the arithmetic is internally consistent in every source. The artifact is TEMPORAL. That GBP10.39 was measured at 31-Dec-2025, signed off 27-Feb-2026, by a CEO and a CFO who have both since resigned, and has not been re-measured through four subsequent negative updates. Stripping goodwill (GBP827.6m) and intangibles (GBP329.2m) gives tangible book GBP6.77/share, P/TB 0.43x; goodwill alone is GBP2.59/share, 89% of the entire share price. FOUR PRIMARY FINDINGS. (1) THE GOODWILL TEST IS REFUTED BY THE COMPANY'S OWN SENSITIVITY TABLE. AR25 Note 11 discloses GBP674m of headroom AND the single-assumption break-points that would take it to nil: volume CAGR falling from 9.1% to 4.6%, adjusted operating margin merely STAYING FLAT at 8.5%, terminal cash conversion falling to 76%, or the discount rate rising to 15.3%. The Directors called none of these 'reasonably possible'. Four months later the 8-Jul-26 update guided to an H1-2026 LOSS of ~GBP30m on heavy discounting and weak affordable-partner demand - which is not a flat 8.5% margin, it is a negative one - with H1 average daily net debt of ~GBP799m against a Board target of NET CASH GBP100m by December. Their own 'severe and unlikely' combined scenario, which still capped margin at 9.8%, produced only a GBP138m impairment; reality is worse than their severe case on the margin leg alone. An impairment on 24 September is close to mechanical. (2) THE NET-DEBT WINDOW DRESSING IS QUANTIFIED AND IT BREAKS THE SCREEN. AR25, verbatim: 'The Group's average daily net debt in 2025 was GBP733.7m (2024: GBP698.1m)' against a reported year-end GBP144.2m - a GBP589.5m, 5.1x gap, repeated in the prior year (3.9x), and worse again at ~GBP799m in H1-26. Re-striking EV on the honest denominator moves EV/EBIT from the shelf's 6.1x to 9.3-9.6x (mcap GBP928.8m + average net debt + GBP98.1m leases + GBP303.6m building-safety provision, over FY25 statutory EBIT GBP222.6m) - and that is against a 2025 EBIT 2026 will not repeat. The same mechanism voids the 19% FCF yield: it is struck on a balance sheet the company observes one day a year. In 2025 they distributed GBP71.2m buying back 11.5m shares while running GBP733.7m of average net debt. (3) THE COVENANT RISK RUNS THROUGH INVENTORY, NOT GOODWILL. Note 20: the RCF, Term Loan and USPP carry interest cover, gearing and TANGIBLE NET WORTH covenants, tested semi-annually. Goodwill sits outside tangible net worth, so an GBP828m write-off is optically violent and covenant-neutral. Inventory does not: Note 18's policy is that 'where the remaining life-of-site margin becomes negative, the full forecast loss is recognised immediately', so press-reported discounting of up to 17% tips whole sites into immediate full-life loss recognition against GBP3,228.3m of gross inventory. And the FY25 going-concern SEVERE-BUT-PLAUSIBLE downside - a further 3% price cut from 1 July 2026, a 7-week completion delay, 5% cancellations, 5% build-cost inflation - was disclosed as producing an outcome where 'the Group would exceed its committed borrowing facilities and breach certain financial covenants' absent mitigations. The discounting leg has been overshot on the company's own July language, four months after the Board approved that scenario. Mitigations are real and mostly in management's control, which is exactly why the buyback stopped in May. (4) THE SHELF POINTED AT THE WRONG NOTE - AN ANTI-MASKING FINDING. The GBP269.8m provision is confirmed as the non-current slice of a GBP379.5m block, of which building safety is GBP213.2m (total building-safety provision GBP303.6m, 230 buildings). Adequacy is BOUNDED and maturing, not deteriorating: the income-statement building-safety expense was GBP114.7m in FY24 and only GBP8.0m in FY25 - Vistry front-loaded in FY24 - and the disclosed sensitivities (+5% buildings = +GBP15.2m, +10% spend = +GBP25.2m) bound the plausible surprise at roughly 13 pence a share against a stock that has lost 456p this year. The cladding note is the cleanest item in the accounts. CONDITIONING: the brief's '17 analysts = no coverage edge' is right about the conclusion and wrong about the reason. The FCA short register (downloaded 2026-08-04, positions dated 8-9 July) shows ~16.7% of shares in issue disclosed net short across 18 holders above the 0.5% floor - Schonfeld 2.44, GLG 2.24, Two Sigma 1.28, Citadel 1.19, BlackRock 0.99 and on - one of the most heavily shorted lines on the UK main market. And the 17 analysts do not agree: targets span 160p to 625p, a 3.9x range, with several models visibly unrevised (forward EPS still carried at 45.3p, ABOVE trailing 42.2p, for a company guiding to a loss - that stale number is the screen's '6.3x forward P/E'). discovery_state = CROWDED with squeeze fuel. Squeeze fuel is a reason not to be short; it is not a reason to be long. HONESTY GRADE: Vistry DISCLOSED all of this - the sensitivity table, the impairment trigger, the average-net-debt gap, the covenant stress are all its own numbers. This is a REJECT on fundamentals, not an EXCLUDE on honesty. What diverges is the FY25 narrative ('signs of stabilisation in Q1 2026', net cash GBP100m by year-end) which was falsified within a week of publication.
